newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian December unemployment rises to 12.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian December unemployment rises to 12.5 pct.

text.p: Unemployment in Bulgaria rose to 478,770 or 12.5 percent of the workforce in December from 460,061 in November, the National Labour Exchange (NLE) said.
"The month-on-month rise in December was mainly due to a fall in the number of seasonal job offers and to lay-offs in state enterprises," NLE chairman Milcho Dimitrov told a news conference.

Bulgaria, hit by a severe economic crisis and preparing for the introduction of a tough monetary regime, has earmarked 64 loss-making state firms for closure under a funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund sealed in July.
Restructuring at some of those enterprises had left some 22,000 people jobless in the last quarter of 1996, Dimitrov said.
Unemployment last year averaged 11.1 percent, down 0.3 percentage points from 1995, NLE figures showed.

A 10 percent cut in public service spending targeted in the 1997 budget draft, yet to be approved by parliament, was expected to boost the number of jobless by at least 50,000 this year, Dimitrov added.
